The feedback inputs are the scaled primary voltage at PA0, isolated
secondary-bulk voltage at PA1, and primary half-bridge-current indication
at PA2. The current signal supports load classification and optional
protection; it is not a measurement of connector output current. ADC
acquisition uses circular DMA and is not synchronized to the carrier.
after:
Primary-voltage feedback is connected to MCU pin PA0, secondary-bulk
feedback to PA1, and half-bridge-current sensing to PA2. The current signal
is used for load classification and optional protection. ADC sampling runs
continuously through circular DMA without synchronization to the carrier.

A charge-pump PFC resonant converter was adapted to a digitally controlled USB-C laboratory supply using inherited planar magnetics. V1 established the power stage and burst-control implementation. Control, sensing, and interface functions were integrated in V2, where lower local heating was observed after tank and timing changes, without establishing higher sustained output. The V3 edge-card design addressed occupied volume, while the remaining winding and input-path losses motivated further magnetic and thermal development.
after: A digitally controlled USB-C laboratory supply was developed from a charge-pump PFC resonant converter and supplied planar magnetics. The first prototype, V1, was used for circuit bring-up and control development. V2 integrated the MCU and associated circuitry on the converter PCB. The V3 edge-card layout was then developed to reduce the converter volume.
